questions.text: What is the definition of an arid climate?

questions.text: The average global temperature increased by 0.6°C in the 20th century.

The Arctic is a continent covered in ice, while Antarctica is an ocean covered in sea ice.

Explain the difference between vollhumid and semihumid climates.
questions.correctAnswer: Vollhumid (fully humid) means sufficient precipitation occurs all year round. Semihumid means sufficient precipitation only during part of the year, with dry periods occurring seasonally.

Describe the ice-albedo feedback loop and explain why it causes the Arctic to warm faster than the global average.
questions.correctAnswer: The ice-albedo feedback loop works as follows: 1) Ice melts and exposes dark ocean water, 2) Dark water has low albedo and absorbs more solar radiation instead of reflecting it, 3) This absorption causes more warming, which leads to more ice melt. This cycle accelerates warming in the Arctic, making it warm approximately twice as fast as the global average.

Compare the Arctic and Antarctic regions, explaining at least four key differences.
questions.correctAnswer: Key differences include: 1) Arctic is an ocean covered by sea ice, while Antarctica is a continent covered by ice; 2) Arctic has approximately 1 million permanent residents, while Antarctica has only about 4,000 research personnel; 3) Arctic is bordered by North America, Asia, and Europe, while Antarctica is isolated by oceans; 4) Arctic sea ice is rapidly shrinking, while Antarctic ice sheets are mostly stable.
